svg.text: Inside one multiply step: a Wallace tree never waits for a carry
A = 2931 (12 bits) x the next 8 multiplier bits (181) + the carry-save accumulator. Each level turns every 3 rows into 2 with full adders.

g.text: level 0: the partial products (multiplicand shifted by j, kept only where multiplier bit j is 1), plus the two accumulator rows
Same-coloured rows go through one row of full adders together: sum = x ^ y ^ z stays in its column, carry = majority(x, y, z) moves one column left.
level 1: 10 rows -> 7 rows (3 rows of full adders in parallel)
Same-coloured rows go through one row of full adders together: sum = x ^ y ^ z stays in its column, carry = majority(x, y, z) moves one column left.
level 2: 7 rows -> 5 rows (2 rows of full adders in parallel)
Same-coloured rows go through one row of full adders together: sum = x ^ y ^ z stays in its column, carry = majority(x, y, z) moves one column left.
level 3: 5 rows -> 4 rows (1 row of full adders in parallel)
Same-coloured rows go through one row of full adders together: sum = x ^ y ^ z stays in its column, carry = majority(x, y, z) moves one column left.
level 4: 4 rows -> 3 rows (1 row of full adders in parallel)
accumulator: carry (passes through) (passes through) (passes through) (passes through)
Same-coloured rows go through one row of full adders together: sum = x ^ y ^ z stays in its column, carry = majority(x, y, z) moves one column left.
level 5: 3 rows -> 2 rows (1 row of full adders in parallel)
Two rows left: in Sixfold they stay two (the carry-save accumulator) until the SIGN cycle, where one prefix adder sums them.
After the last step: one carry-propagate adder (Kogge-Stone) turns the two rows into the product
2931 x 181 + 421 + 244 = 531176 (checked when this picture was drawn)
5 levels of one full adder each: no carry ever travels more than one column before the final add.
The real step (src/Carry_Save_Multiplier.sv) does 64 x 16 bits: 18 rows -> 2 in 6 levels, every clock cycle.
